title: Sum of the first odd integers
statement: For every integer n >= 1, the sum of the first n positive odd integers is n^2.
candidate_proof: Use induction. For n=1 the sum is 1=1^2. Assume 1+3+...+(2n-1)=n^2. Adding the next odd integer gives n^2+(2n+1)=(n+1)^2. The claim follows for every n >= 1.
verification_rules: Check the base case and the induction step.
Reject a proof that establishes the identity for only selected values of n.

title: False universal statement about primes
candidate_proof: A prime has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself. An even number is divisible by 2, so a prime cannot be even. Therefore every prime is odd.
verification_rules: Test the universal claim at the smallest prime.
Treat one counterexample as decisive.

title: Zero-product claim without an integral-domain assumption
statement: For every commutative ring R and all a,b in R, ab=0 implies a=0 or b=0.
candidate_proof: Suppose ab=0 and a is nonzero. Divide both sides by a to obtain b=0. Thus a=0 or b=0.
verification_rules: Check whether division by a nonzero element is available in the stated ring.
Look for a counterexample with nonzero zero divisors.

title: Swapped quantifiers in an unboundedness claim
statement: There exists an integer y such that for every integer x, y > x.
candidate_proof: Given any integer x, choose y=x+1. Then y>x. Hence there is an integer y larger than every integer x.
verification_rules: Preserve the order of existential and universal quantifiers.
Require one fixed witness for an existential quantifier outside a universal quantifier.

title: Square-root identity with the wrong domain conclusion
statement: For every real number x, sqrt(x^2)=x.
candidate_proof: Squaring and square-rooting are inverse operations, so sqrt(x^2)=x for every real x.
verification_rules: Use the principal nonnegative square root.
Check the claim for a negative real input.

title: Correct irrationality conclusion with a false parity inference
statement: The square root of 2 is irrational.
candidate_proof: Assume sqrt(2)=a/b in lowest terms. Then a^2=2b^2, so a is even. Since a and b are coprime, they must have the same parity, and b is therefore even. This contradicts lowest terms, so sqrt(2) is irrational.
verification_rules: Check each parity inference rather than accepting the known conclusion.
Reject the claim that coprime integers must have the same parity.

title: Circular proof of infinitely many primes
statement: There are infinitely many prime numbers.
candidate_proof: Assume the theorem that every finite list of primes omits another prime. If there were only finitely many primes, list all of them. The assumed theorem supplies a prime outside that list, a contradiction. Therefore there are infinitely many primes.
verification_rules: Reject use of a lemma equivalent to the target unless the proof establishes it independently.
Trace the dependency of every decisive premise.

title: A decisive quadratic-residue lemma left unproved
statement: There are infinitely many primes congruent to 1 modulo 4.
candidate_proof: Suppose p1,...,pk are all primes congruent to 1 modulo 4 and let N=(2p1...pk)^2+1. Every prime divisor q of N is congruent to 1 modulo 4. No pi divides N, so q is a new prime congruent to 1 modulo 4, a contradiction.
verification_rules: Require a proof that every odd prime divisor of x^2+1 is 1 modulo 4.
Reject an unsupported key lemma even if the theorem is true.

title: Invalid exchange of limit and integral
statement: lim(n to infinity) integral_0^1 n*x^(n-1) dx = 0.
candidate_proof: For each x in [0,1), n*x^(n-1) tends to 0, and the exceptional endpoint x=1 has measure zero. Exchange the limit and integral to obtain the integral of 0, which is 0.
verification_rules: Check the integral before accepting an exchange of limit and integration.
Require a valid convergence theorem with all hypotheses verified.

title: Reversed inequality in a harmonic-number bound
candidate_proof: For k>=2, the function 1/x is decreasing, so 1/k >= integral from k-1 to k of 1/x. Summing gives H_n <= 1+integral from 1 to n of 1/x = 1+ln(n).
verification_rules: Check the direction of the pointwise integral comparison.
Require the summed inequality to follow from the displayed inequalities.

title: Boundary case omitted from a nonnegativity proof
statement: For every real number x, x^2 >= 0.
candidate_proof: If x>0, then x*x>0. If x<0, the product of the two negative factors x and x is positive. Thus x^2>=0 for every real x.
verification_rules: Check that the proof covers x=0.
Reject a case split that omits a value in the stated domain.

title: Semantic mutation deleting the decisive induction calculation
statement: For every integer n >= 1, the sum of the first n positive odd integers is n^2.
candidate_proof: Use induction. For n=1 the sum is 1=1^2. Assume 1+3+...+(2n-1)=n^2. Add the next odd integer. The claim follows for every n >= 1.
verification_rules: Require the induction step to derive the n+1 case from the n case.
Treat a missing algebraic transition as a proof gap.

title: Semantic mutation replacing a universal induction claim with one witness
statement: For every integer n >= 1, the sum of the first n positive odd integers is n^2.
candidate_proof: Choose n=1. The sum of the first one odd integer is 1=1^2, so there exists n for which the formula holds. Therefore the formula holds for every n >= 1.
verification_rules: Distinguish existence of one witness from a universal conclusion.
Reject a proof that swaps the required quantifiers.

Verify the displayed algebraic identity symbol by symbol.

title: Semantic mutation replacing the induction hypothesis
statement: For every integer n >= 1, the sum of the first n positive odd integers is n^2.
candidate_proof: Use induction. For n=1 the sum is 1=1^2. For the induction step assume 1+3+...+(2n-1)=n^2+1. Adding 2n+1 gives (n+1)^2+1, which proves the desired formula.
verification_rules: Require the induction hypothesis to match the proposition being proved.
Reject a substituted assumption that changes the equality.
